subject: EU/APAC traffic segmentation & residency cutover — notice + validation
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acme-financial.com
Date: 2027-09-06T08:23:00Z
Subject: EU/APAC traffic segmentation & residency cutover — notice + validation

Team / Acme ops,

We have a planned cutover window for the EU → APAC warm-standby segmentation on Saturday 2027-09-18 02:00–06:00 UTC. This is a controlled traffic segmentation exercise — NOT a full switchover — intended to validate our residency controls when failover routing is engaged. High level: 

- Warm standby in APAC will receive mirrored traffic via regional proxy; no persistent storage will be written there during the exercise.
- BGP announcements will be adjusted and DNS TTL lowered to 30s prior to the window.
- KMS keys for EU-custodied logs will remain in the EU; access patterns will be logged and audited.

Action items for our side (please confirm):
1) Network ACLs and peering: confirm that peering to the APAC standby only allows ingress from the proxy subnets listed in the attachment (network-diagram-v2.pdf).
2) Egress guardrails: ensure egress ACLs block any session that would route non-EU PII out of EU zones during the exercise.
3) DNS/BGP plan: verify TTL, withdraw/announce schedule and the test rollback plan.
4) Monitoring + forensic capture: enable packet capture (30 min max) on the proxy and ship logs to EU-resident S3 for the window.

@Aditya — can you validate the KV cache behavior under mirrored requests (we want to ensure no KV eviction causes unexpected writes)?
@Lauren — can you confirm legal/compliance is comfortable with the packet-capture scope and retention?
@Soojin — can you review the BGP/DNS runbook and sign off on the rollout/rollback steps?

I've attached the network diagram and the configuration checklist. Ops at Acme, please confirm any compliance constraints we should incorporate into the runbook.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: network-diagram-v2.pdf (PDF), config-checklist.csv (CSV)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Date: 2027-09-06T12:10:00Z
Subject: Re: EU/APAC traffic segmentation & residency cutover — notice + validation

Thanks Karthik — quick read and a couple clarifications: 

- DNS TTL: lowering to 30s is fine; we should push an announce/withdraw schedule to the ops team 48h in advance and a final pre-check 2h before the window.
- BGP prep: confirm with networking that communities are set to prefer EU paths unless failover trigger is met.
- For packet capture: compliance OK with ephemeral captures limited to proxies, provided hashes are redacted prior to any export.

From: maria.gonzalez@acme-financial.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acme-financial.com
Date: 2027-09-07T09:32:00Z
Subject: Re: EU/APAC traffic segmentation & residency cutover — notice + validation

Karthik / Lauren / Aditya,

Thanks for the heads up. A few compliance constraints from Acme's side: 

- During any failover or test that involves traffic crossing regions, we require an attestation that no EU-resident customer PII is written to non-EU storage. We need the technical control details in advance.
- Packet captures are acceptable if we receive a redaction plan and evidence that only proxy headers and metadata are captured.
- We will need a 72-hour window to file an internal change notice and confirm our SOC2 custodian.

Can you provide the exact BGP announce timeline, the list of CIDRs that will be permitted to the APAC standby, and confirm KMS key policies for the exercise? Attached is a template (sox-evidence-request.xlsx) for the artifacts our audit team will expect after the test.

Regards,
María González
Platform Ops — Acme Financial
maría.gonzalez@acme-financial.com

--
Attachment stub: sox-evidence-request.xlsx (XLSX)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: maria.gonzalez@acme-financial.com, ops@acme-financial.com
Date: 2027-09-09T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: EU/APAC traffic segmentation & residency cutover — notice + validation (final prep + runbook links)

All — thanks for the fast turnaround. Short answers and next steps below.

1) BGP/DNS timeline (final): 
   - 2027-09-16 10:00 UTC: DNS TTL pre-lower (24h notice).
   - 2027-09-17 22:00 UTC: DNS TTL set to 30s; final pre-check.
   - 2027-09-18 02:00 UTC: Begin mirrored traffic to APAC proxy via announced community (no write-to-disk paths).
   - 2027-09-18 05:45 UTC: Rollback announcement and verify EU path preference.

2) CIDRs and ACLs: see attached network-diagram-v2.pdf and config-checklist.csv — permitted APAC proxy CIDRs are listed in section 'ProxyIngress'. We will block any egress to public non-EU S3 endpoints during the window.

3) KMS keys: all customer-facing keys remain in the EU account; any ephemeral keys used for the APAC proxy have no access to persistent storage. Key policy snapshots are linked in the runbook.

4) Packet-capture & evidence: we will run 30-minute captures limited to proxy interface; hashes will be calculated in-EU and redaction applied before any external transfer. Post-test deliverables aligned with your SOX template: packet-capture hashes, KMS policy snapshot, BGP announce logs, and ACL change diffs.

Runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-residency-runbook
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-42

Can Acme ops confirm the 72h internal notice requirement is satisfied on your side? Once confirmed we'll lock the schedule and run tabletop on 2027-09-15.

— Karthik
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
